settings.name_in_paper: Causal bandit with unknown causal graph (cumulative regret)
unmapped: Arms are interventions do(X=x) on subsets of n nodes of an unknown causal DAG, each variable taking K values; reward node R not intervenable
Learner observes all variables of the PCM after each intervention (not only the reward)
Causal DAG is unknown (no essential graph known); no hidden confounders
Ancestoral effect identifiability (eps) and reward identifiability (Delta) assumptions
The learner knows the identifiability thresholds eps and Delta, the number of nodes n and the domain size K
settings.definition_quote:
In a causal bandit \cite{lattimore2016causal}, a learner $\cL$ performs a set
of interventions, i.e. actions, at each round $t\in[T]$ by setting a subset of
variables $\bX_t=(X_1,\dots,X_\ell)\subseteq\cV$ to some values
$\bx_t\in[K]^{\ell}$, denoted by $\doop(\bX_t=\bx_t)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Causal bandit with unknown causal graph (simple regret)
unmapped: Arms are interventions on subsets of nodes of an unknown causal DAG with K-valued variables
Learner observes all variables after each intervention
Ancestoral effect identifiability (eps) and reward identifiability (Delta) assumptions
The learner knows eps, Delta, n and K
settings.definition_quote: simple regret which only focuses on the reward of the final intervention, predicted to be the best by the learner after T interactions

settings.name_in_paper: Parent node discovery with atomic interventions (number of distinct node interventions)
unmapped: Goal is to identify the parent node(s) of the reward node in an unknown causal DAG; performance measured as the expected number of distinct nodes intervened on
Each intervention on a node is assumed to reveal its descendants and whether it is an ancestor of the parent (idealised; statistical cost handled separately)
settings.definition_quote: We denote the parent node by P ... and denote the number of distinct nodes intervened on by our algorithm by N(G,P).

settings.name_in_paper: Parent node discovery with atomic interventions (lower bound)
unmapped: Goal is to identify the parent node of the reward node; measured by expected number of distinct node interventions
Learner may know the graph G up to a uniformly random relabeling of nodes
Each intervention reveals descendants / ancestry of the parent exactly

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote:
Assume that $\cP\neq\emptyset$, i.e., the reward variable has at least one
parent in $\cV$. For the learner that uses \cref{alg:multiparent} and then runs
a \acs{ucb} the following bound\footnote{$f(n)\preceq g(n)$ stands for an
inequality up to a universal constant.} for the conditional regret holds with
probability at least $1-\delta$:
\begin{align}
\hspace{-.25cm}R_{\cL}^T(\bcG,P\mid E)
\!\leq \!\max\cbr{\frac1{\Delta^2},\frac1{\eps^2}}\!
K^{\abs\cP+1}\E[N(\bcG,\cP)]\log\pr{\!\frac{nK^n}{\delta}\!}

results.notes: Regret is 'conditional regret' given event E that the parent set is correctly found (P(E)>=1-delta); defined through expected rewards. Inequality holds up to a universal constant per footnote, hence O.

tuning: final intervention sampled from empirical distribution of played interventions

source.label: thm:log-condition
source.quote:
Assume that $\bcG$ is such that for any $\cC\in\bcC_{\bcG}(P)$
at least one of the following holds
i) $\abs{\cH_\cC(\alpha)}\geq\beta\abs{\cC}$,
ii) $\abs{\cA_\cC(P)}\geq\gamma\abs{\cC}$, or
iii) $\abs\cC\leq c\log^k(n)$,





for fixed $0<\alpha,\beta,\gamma<1$, $c\in\R_{>0}$, and $k\geq1$.
Then, $\E[N(\bcG,P)]=\cO(\log^k n).$

conditions: G is an Erdos-Renyi random DAG with p_edge >= 1 - ((1-c)/(log^k n - 1))^{1/(log^k n - 1)}, c in [0,1]
condition of Theorem log-condition holds in expectation

source.label: corollary:erdos-renyi
source.quote:
The family of Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random \acp{dag} satisfies the
condition of \cref{thm:log-condition} in expectation if
$p\geq1-\pr{\frac{1-c}{\log^kn-1}}^{1/(\log^kn-1)}$, for any
constant $c\in[0,1]$. Therefore, for such graphs, \ac{raps} requires

$\E[N(\bcG,P)]=\cO(\log^k n)$

expected number of interventions.

symbols.d_deg: maximum degree in the skeleton of G

conditions: at most O(n/log_d n) nodes X != P that are disconnected from P or have all paths to P blocked by colliders

source.label: thm:sublinear
source.quote:
Let $\bcG$ be an arbitrary \ac{dag} in which there are at most
$\cO\pr{\frac{n}{\log_d(n)}}$ nodes $X\in\cV\setminus\cbr{P}$ such
that either $P$ is disconnected with $X$, or all paths between
$P$ and $X$ are blocked by colliders.  Then,
$
\E[N(\bcG,P)]=\cO\pr{\frac{n}{\log_d n}},
$
where $d$ is the maximum degree in the skeleton of $\bcG$.

results.notes: Slow regime; tight for d-ary trees per text.

source.quote:
Let $\bcG_{n,p}$ be an Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph with
$p\geq1-\pr{\frac{1-c_0}{\log^k(c_1\log^k(n))-1}}^{

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote:
Fix a causal graph $\bcG$ and a parent node $P$. Any learner $\cL$ that
correctly identifies the parent node $P$, for any graph obtained from $\bcG$ by
relabeling\footnote{Relableing corresponds to the assignment of indices 1
through $n$ identifying each node, but not the assignment of random variables
to nodes.}of the nodes and having $P$ take one of $n$ vertices or
$P=\varnothing$, satisfies
\begin{equation*}
\E[N_{\cL}(\bcG,P)]\geq
\sum_{X\in\cV}\frac1{
\abs{\cA_{\bcG}(P)\triangle\cA_{\bcG}(X)\setminus\cbr{X}}+1},
\end{equation*}

results.notes: Matches the exact RAPS expression (Theorem exact). Text derives Omega(n/log_d n) for d-ary trees and Omega(n) for null/collider graphs (not separate formal statements).
